additionalRepairConsidered.finding: Public Policy Analysis offers relevant policy methods, but no planned 2026–2029 offering is marked in the workbook. It is not selected; an unavailable course cannot repair the programme.

academicReview.closestResponse: Retain the substantial biomedical programme. Its response rests on sustained anatomy, normal function, cell/biochemistry, mechanisms of disease, immunity, pathology, pharmacology, cognition, health psychology and scientific methods—not merely a coherent label or a clinical-training disclaimer.
academicReview.strongestCounterargument: Medicine integrates biomedical knowledge with patient care and clinical professional competence throughout. The UCR programmes lack that integration; they must not be described as medical training. This limitation is consequential but does not remove the demonstrated scientific response to the medical bachelor’s defining biomedical substance.
academicReview.relatedDirections: Retain technology: substantial biomedical teaching plus explicitly evidenced technology methods and actual medical-imaging/clinical-AI ethics contributions. Repair population health by retaining 18 of 24 courses and replacing six weak/disproportionate additions with relevant biomedical/health courses; its organising difference remains prevention, population evidence and social organisation.
academicReview.clinicalCandidate: The eight patient-facing generator interests are grouped coherently and rejected as a sustained UCR clinical-practice direction. They are no longer silently marked as fulfilled by the closest core.

stoppingDecision.assessment: The closest option substantively owns biomedical foundations, illness experience/lifespan, ethical issues in biomedical research and scientific inquiry. The patient-facing clinical-practice cluster is explicitly rejected as a UCR direction: the current courses do not sustain medical interviewing, physical examinations, clinical case management or supervised patient care. Those interests are not claimed as fulfilled by general rhetoric or health psychology. This does not invalidate the strongest academic biomedical response: 21 of its courses are in health, cognition and behavioural science, with statistics and social analysis supporting them. The evidence-backed technology direction retains a substantial biomedical base and adds computational methods, imaging and responsible AI. The population-health direction has been repaired to combine health science and prevention with population, behavioural and organisational analysis. All three pass substantive and numerical distinctness: they differ by 11, 7 and 15 courses in the respective pairs. Three is the maximum reached after these checks, not a preset target; the clinical-practice candidate remains rejected.

externalReview.identity: Full-time Dutch-taught BSc Geneeskunde, Erasmus MC / Erasmus University Rotterdam, CROHO 56551; Erasmusarts2030, ordinary programme, no formal specialist route.
externalReview.coverage: 13 integrated blocks, four projects, five longitudinal lines, 30-EC broadening minor, integrated final works and 1-EC professionalism, all accounted for once.
externalReview.creditMethod: 60/60/30/29/1 are workload/coverage accounting groups. They are not invented block EC or a claim that 60 EC is awarded annually. Official award timing is 30 EC after the Ba1 decision, 30 EC minor, remainder at final examination.
externalReview.progressionAndConditions: Current 2026–2027 Erasmusarts 2030 OER and appendices govern this full-time Dutch-taught 180-EC Bachelor Geneeskunde (CROHO 56551). Partial English teaching supports the literature; the normalized target is not an English or part-time route. No formal specialist bachelor track is selected; the ordinary programme is retained, not the separate individually approved vrij onderwijsprogramma. Appendix 2 articles 9–10 and table 2 define 13 integrated case-based blocks, four projects and five longitudinal lines: clinical skills, identity/professionalism, social engagement, academic formation and technology. Workload is evenly spread across three years; the five display components retain 60 EC of Year-1 workload, 60 EC of Year-2 workload, 30 EC minor, 29 EC of final integrated study and the separately specified 1 EC of longitudinal professionalism. These are workload/coverage accounting groups, not official separately credited year courses: only 30 EC is awarded at the first-year progression decision, 30 EC after the minor, and the remaining credits at the final examination to reach 180. The 1 EC of professionalism is included, not added to 180; its final-year placement is an accounting convention because it is awarded at the examination. No EC is invented for individual themes, projects, competencies or assessments. The clinical skills and professional lines are compulsory integrated teaching. Year 3 includes competency-linked final works within its integrated blocks; the Medical Science project is not a separately credited thesis. OER article 4.4 requires 30 EC of broadening minor study: an eligible 30-EC minor or at least 15 EC plus another minor or approved university electives; external institutions outside the named EUR/TU Delft/Leiden group and all elective packages require prior Examination Board permission. OER article 4.1 and appendices 3–6 govern progression: a favourable decision and 30-EC BSA at the end of Ba1, another favourable decision before the minor, and a further decision before Block 11. These involve block-test and competency standards, professional conduct and iVTG participation/POP reflections, rather than ordinary 60-EC yearly completion thresholds. Final requirements include all block tests attempted, none below level, all competencies at level, iVTG level 12 in Ba3, completed BLS2 and no active remediation process. The public marketing reference to 35 or 30 ECTS does not override the adopted 30-EC EA2030 norm. The journey diagram confirms the block/project order; its project-4 label Management is descriptive, while the OER label Organisation controls. No clinical licence or medical-master admission is inferred for UCR.

findings: The strongest challenge is the absence of sustained clinical practice, which is central to Medicine. A disclaimer alone cannot cure an academically weak comparison. Here the closest programme has sustained actual health-science content: 21 Health/Cognition/Behaviour courses cover anatomical structure, physiology, cellular/biochemical mechanisms, pathology, infection, pharmacology, neuroscience, psychology, population evidence and research. The positive conclusion rests on that substantive scientific response, not on coherence alone or access to a profession.

The eight patient-facing interests are now explicitly assigned to one rejected clinical-practice candidate. The final text does not claim general rhetoric, theoretical psychology or lab work delivers medical interviewing, physical examination or patient case management.

The technology programme has a real biomedical anchor plus mathematical/computational methods and documented medical-imaging/clinical-AI-ethics contributions. General databases, algorithms, neural networks and robotics are represented as methods; no clinical specialism is invented.

The population-health repair preserves 18 courses and removes six unsupported/disproportionate links. Its epidemiology, health psychology, infection, disease science and research now substantiate the health object; the economic, social and organisational courses provide explicit complementary tools. The seven-course difference from the closest programme follows the concept, not threshold-filling.

All 72 placements, programme totals, advanced/PPD rules, traceability, pairwise distinctness and status-appropriate formal/audience schemas passed. Three corrected modal descriptions now follow actual enriched profiles and avoid clinical-training or categorical master-admission claims.

Whole external-year rows remain partial curricular relationships, clearly labelled as workload groups with clinical/project content beyond the single UCR course beside them. All five groups cover the full programme once; optional UCR research remains separate from scheduled 180 EC.
